prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Design the INSTRUMENT MODES of CLEAN TUNER as a beautiful TWO PANEL side by side portrait app screen study. Reference image establishes the approved exact aesthetic: frosted champagne silver shell, soft recessed ivory glass, charcoal fine typography, subtle warm amber light, minimal precise contemporary analog gear. Carry over its thin segmented arch note RANGE display. New instrument UI below it. Landscape board with two matching tall screens, no phones, no hands, orthographic, no tilt. Warm grey backdrop. Small exterior captions GUITAR and UKULELE.

Each screen: small CLEAN TUNER header top left, one tiny settings icon top right. Just below header a quiet horizontal instrument and tuning selector: left screen "Guitar ▾" and "Standard ▾"; right "Ukulele ▾" and "High G ▾". These are restrained text controls, no heavy buttons.
Top half inset main display: a shallow arched ribbon consisting of THREE translucent ivory note zones, thin and graceful, not chunky. NO ruler ticks, NO fixed center line. Only two subtle seams at boundaries halfway between note labels. Left screen zones labeled G♯ / A₂ / A♯, A₂ centered at apex. A single short thin amber actual-pitch marker slightly left of center (-8 cents) with soft local glow. Under arc compact "-8 ct" and "FLAT". Right screen zones labeled B / C₄ / C♯, C₄ centered at apex, amber actual-pitch marker at exact center, compact "0 ct" and "IN TUNE". Small LOW / HIGH at arc ends. Selected target stays centered in instrument mode.

Lower half of EACH screen: carefully rendered beautifully restrained front-facing instrument HEADSTOCK illustration, a warm pearl/silver etched relief, no wood grain, no full guitar body. Tiny real-looking metallic tuning pegs and fine strings routed to their posts, soft shadows. Headstock must be visibly integrated into interface, not a decorative photograph. Six-string guitar on left with EXACTLY three tuning machines each side, four-string ukulele on right with EXACTLY two machines each side. Straight short neck emerges downwards, strings visible. Place legible labeled touch targets beside the corresponding pegs, without crossing lines, as follows:
Guitar 3+3 headstock: LEFT SIDE from bottom (nearest nut) to top: "6 E₂", "5 A₂", "4 D₃". RIGHT SIDE from top to bottom (nearest nut): "3 G₃", "2 B₃", "1 E₄". Exactly six labels. Highlight ONLY "5 A₂" with a very subtle warm amber halo and its string glowing faintly, all others quiet charcoal. Physical strings at nut from viewer left to right E₂ A₂ D₃ G₃ B₃ E₄.
Ukulele 2+2 headstock: LEFT SIDE bottom to top: "4 G₄", "3 C₄". RIGHT SIDE top to bottom: "2 E₄", "1 A₄". Exactly four labels. Highlight ONLY "3 C₄" and its string faint amber. Standard reentrant high G tuning, not low G.
Small understated "AUTO" near top of headstock area denotes automatic string recognition, not a giant control. Bottom footer tiny listening indicator + "Listening" on left and "A4 440 Hz" on right. Listening is STATUS ONLY. No big microphone button. Avoid extra menus, decorative screws, wood, green smileys, duplicate big note names, dense dashboard information. Entire design consistent and compact with premium material details, warm and modern not vintage. Enough space for the headstock controls to read clearly. This should feel like two modes of the same refined app in the reference, with a functional instrument diagram and accessible tuning selector.

interaction.automatic: Detect likely string from selected tuning.
interaction.manual: Tap a string to lock its target; return to Auto explicitly.
interaction.tuning: Instrument tuning selector changes target pitches and diagram labels.

review: String labels and tuning peg counts correct. Guitar string routing/glow is illustrative and must be corrected in deterministic implementation; marker angle is not calibrated.
